versions.name: RXV2-0.9.674-help-arrow
versions.notes: The help screen's way out is now the SAME round back arrow as every page, in the same top-left corner, instead of the wide bar 0.9.673 used. It floats above the overlay so it is there however far the help is scrolled. Got it stays at the bottom, tapping outside and Escape still work. The test compares its size, shape, colour and arrow against the page back button rule by rule. Includes 0.9.673.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.673-help-back
versions.notes: Every help screen now has a Back button at the TOP that stays there while you scroll, so opening one by mistake no longer means scrolling to the bottom to get out (Malcolm asked). Got it stays at the bottom for anyone who reads to the end, tapping outside still closes, and Escape now does too. The help panel is a solid colour, as everything else on these pages is. Includes 0.9.672.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.672-keep-checks
versions.notes: Every finished check is now kept on the phone - the last six per model, about 30 kB each - and any of them can be opened again with no cable and no helicopter. So erasing the black box costs nothing, and a flight can be looked at again after a filter change. A kept check is clearly marked and can change nothing; run a new one for that. Page only, no firmware behaviour changed. Includes 0.9.671.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.671-flight-review
versions.notes: See the flight, not just its vibration. The check now decodes head speed, the governor's wanted speed, throttle, battery volts and current, roll and pitch, ESC temperature and motor RPM as it reads, and the page shows them as a stack of traces sharing one time axis, with arming, governor changes and rescue marked - plus a plain-English summary ('Head speed averaged 1325 rpm, dipping to 1270. The governor asked for 1300, so it held to within 25 rpm. Battery 25.0 V down to 23.4 V, sagging to 22.8 V under load.'). A link to What to record on the Flight recorder page sits on the check page, since that is where you notice a field is missing. Includes 0.9.670.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.670-memory-card
versions.notes: Vibration check page: a Black box memory card of its own - a bar and a plain 'X of Y used (Z%)' line, and an 'Erase all flight logs' button right there, refused while armed or with the rotor turning and confirmed first. When the memory is over half full it says how much time erasing would save, because that is where you notice it. The Flight recorder page keeps its own copy of both. Includes 0.9.669.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.669-bank-handover
versions.notes: Defence in depth on the bank hazard: a check already cannot start while the flight controller's banks are still held (0.9.667), but the vibration check's stand-down in bankPutBackTick now sits BELOW the transmitter hand-over instead of above it, so a transmitter switched on during a check still reaches the branch that releases the hold and records where the flight controller was left. Only the MSP work waits. And when the link is handed back, an owed put-back is attempted at once instead of after the two-second back-off. Includes 0.9.668.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.668-armed-recheck
versions.notes: FLIGHT SAFETY: the vibration check's once-a-second 'is it armed?' re-check never actually ran while the black box was streaming - it lived only on the idle path, and a healthy stream re-arms the next read immediately, so the flight controller's armed word was read once at the start and then frozen. On a receiver the transmitter test still covered it; on a DONGLE nothing did. All 'what next?' decisions now go through one place that gives the armed re-check its turn. Also: the idle watchdog now leaves exactly the state stopLink() leaves (a latched mspAsyncFunc would have confused the transmitter-parameter machine), and the serial MSP parser is reset when a read times out and whenever the USB device comes or goes, so one dropped byte cannot hold it open for a whole 4 kB reply. Includes 0.9.667.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.667-banks-first
versions.notes: FLIGHT SAFETY, found by the pre-flight review: a vibration check stands the bank put-back down for its whole run, so if a phone session had left the flight controller on a different PID bank and the transmitter came on during the check, the put-back was abandoned and the model would have flown on the phone's bank. A check now refuses to start while the banks are still held, and while any page has talked to the flight controller in the last 5 seconds (a restore is many requests with gaps); the page waits and retries by itself, so it is invisible. Also: the 20-minute cap now bounds the whole run, not each widened pass. Includes 0.9.666.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.666-check-watchdog
versions.notes: Two safety nets before the Goblin flies: bbCheckActive (which stands every other MSP sender down) can never outlive the check that set it - the idle tick clears it and says so in the log; and a check that somehow ran past 20 minutes hands the flight controller back. Nothing in the flight path changed: Radio.h, Channels.h, Output.h, Telemetry.h and FlightLog.h are untouched since before the vibration check existed. Includes 0.9.665.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.665-check-goblin
versions.notes: Vibration check, corrected by the Goblin's own flight: it advised 'set the rotor-speed notches to high' for a once-per-rev that Rotorflight's NORMAL preset already notches - the change would have done nothing. The check now knows what each preset really notches (rpmFilterPreset[] in rpm_filter.c: main harmonics 1-2-4 low, 1-4 normal, 1-6 high, tail 1 / 1-2 / 1-2, plus the main motor) and only advises a preset that genuinely adds the harmonic; a strong once-per-rev is reported as blade tracking and balance, with no filter button. Attenuation is measured over a wider window so a narrow rotor notch is not mistaken for a useless one. The 90-second Goblin flight is now a regression fixture (dev/goblin_flight_*.json). Includes 0.9.664.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.664-check-window
versions.notes: Vibration check reads the last 12 MB of the black box (the newest flight or two) instead of the whole memory, widening itself if that holds no log, and shows a time remaining; the page says so and offers Erase. Measured throughput 62-66 kB/s.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.663-check-fast
versions.notes: Vibration check: the armed gate no longer aborts the check before the flight controller has answered (and never forces the shared armed flag every page reads); reads 4096-byte chunks where the FC allows, through the check's own PSRAM buffer.
